submission.natural_language_explanation: A pure token detector (layer 0, no context): fires on noun-preceding determiner words. It is strongest on English possessive and demonstrative determiners in any case: ' this' (max 2.1), ' your', ' their', ' our', ' his', ' its' (about 1.9-2.1), ' my', ' her', ' these', ' thy', 'This'/'The'/'Your' forms (1.3-1.6). It also fires on ' the'/'The' (about 1.4-1.5), ' those', ' each', ' every', ' any', ' some', ' whose', ' an', ' another' (0.5-1.2), and on foreign determiners such as ' cette', ' notre', ' votre', ' leur', ' la', ' los', 'その', 'この', '这'. It is inactive (below 0.25 of max) on ' that' (0), ' a', 'A'/' A', ' which', ' many', ' few', ' most', ' all', ' both', ' several', on subject and object pronouns (' he', ' you', ' I', ' him', ' them', ' me'; ' we', ' they' and ' it' sit just at the line, about 0.55-0.6), and on all nouns, verbs, prepositions, conjunctions and punctuation.

rival_explanations: A narrower superlative/ordinal-frame reading: the pole fires on ' the' mainly when it introduces a superlative or ordinal ('the first', 'the best', 'the same'), so definite noun phrases before ordinary nouns should be weak or inactive.

A narrower determiner-class reading: the pole fires on the definite article and the possessives ('his', 'her', 'its', 'our', 'their', 'your') but not on demonstratives ('this', 'these', 'those') or quantifiers ('each', 'every', 'some', 'any', 'another'), which sit at this pole's floor.

A lookahead reading: the pole fires in the determiner slot to boost an upcoming superlative or ordinal ('the strongest', 'the first'), so its peaks prepare the following word and ablating it should cost that word probability rather than reacting to the determiner.
